Method of Attack: Speculative execution side-channel data-sampling attacks leaking data from CPU buffers
Exploits vulnerabilities in Intel CPUs to leak data from internal CPU buffers such as Line-Fill Buffers, Load Ports, Store Buffers, and Fill Buffers
Leverages Microarchitectural Data Sampling (MDS) vulnerabilities to extract sensitive information including passwords, cryptographic keys, and kernel data
Discoverer: VUSec (Vrije University Amsterdam and CISPA Helmholtz Center for Information Security) for RIDL

University of Michigan, University of Adelaide, Worcester Polytechnic Institute, Data61, Graz Institute of Applied Information Processing and Communications (IAIK), Catholic University in Leuven (KU Leuven) for Fallout
Security researchers who disclosed ZombieLoad alongside RIDL and Fallout
Impacted Systems: Intel CPUs released since 2008 including 9th generation processors
Systems running vulnerable Intel processors including servers, laptops, desktops, cloud infrastructures
Operating systems with kernel and user-space processes, Software Guard Extensions (SGX) enclaves
Attack Vector: Running unprivileged malicious code on vulnerable machines
Malicious JavaScript on webpages or advertisements
Date of Discovery: Late January 2019 (Fallout attack researchers contacted Intel)
Indicators of Compromise: Videos demonstrating data leaks from /etc/shadow, /proc/version, and JavaScript/WebAssembly processes
